title: Degreewise unbounded exchange invertibility on one etale chart
statement: Use the chosen Cartesian squares and canonical exchange arrows of [sbc-def-base-change-square] and [sbc-def-base-change-map]. Let Y to X, Y to T, X to S, T to S be a global Cartesian square. Let a:U to X and b:V to S be etale, fi:U to V satisfy fi followed by b=a followed by f, and let c:T' to T, gi:T' to V give a Cartesian square over g,b. Let hi:Y' to U and ei:Y' to T' be any chosen Cartesian square over fi,gi. For any unbounded complex K on T_et and any integer q, if H^q of the local abelian derived exchange at D(c inverse image)K is invertible, then a inverse image of H^q of the global exchange at K is invertible. Exact inverse image induces the functor D as in [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. There is no covering or joint-surjectivity assumption. The fibre products are those of [def-pc-fibre-product]. The chosen Cartesian representatives are arbitrary.

proof.text: Etale extension by zero is left Kan extension followed by sheafification. Its left exactness follows from the discrete lift description of the Kan extension and exact coproducts in abelian groups. It is a left adjoint, hence right exact. Its right adjoint, etale inverse image, preserves K-injective complexes by the exact-left-adjoint criterion.

proof.text: Ordinary etale exchange is invertible by the source localization-restriction comparison. Apply the exact-adjoint derived-mate compatibility theorem to derive this isomorphism on unbounded categories. Verify its pasted-unit hypothesis explicitly from the two right-derived composition factorization equations, cancelling the ordinary comparison isomorphism. The conjugate composition formula identifies the resulting right-adjoint square with the conjugate of the prescribed derived inverse-image square.

proof.text: Apply mapDerivedCategoryNatIso to ordinary inverse-image associativity; its whiskering and composition coherence give the associativity needed by mate pasting. Compute the outer rectangle through the local square and hc, and through the global square and the square d,hi,h,a. Apply degree-q homology and cancel all invertible factors from the two etale exchange maps. The exact-functor homology isomorphism identifies homology after derived inverse image with ordinary inverse image after homology. No bound on K or q is used.

theorem abelianDerivedBaseChangeArrow_local_homology_isIso
    {X Y S T U V T' Y' : Scheme.{u}}
    {h : Y ⟶ X} {e : Y ⟶ T} {f : X ⟶ S} {g : T ⟶ S}
    (sq : ChosenCartesianSquare h e f g)
    (a : U ⟶ X) [AlgebraicGeometry.Etale a]
    (fi : U ⟶ V) (b : V ⟶ S) [AlgebraicGeometry.Etale b]
    (wfactor : fi ≫ b = a ≫ f)
    (c : T' ⟶ T) (gi : T' ⟶ V) (hc : IsPullback c gi g b)
    {ei : Y' ⟶ T'} {hi : Y' ⟶ U}
    (localSquare : ChosenCartesianSquare hi ei fi gi)
    (K : DerivedCategory (Sheaf T.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})) (q : ℤ)
    (hK : IsIso ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ q).map
      (abelianDerivedBaseChangeArrow localSquare
        (D(upperStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} c).obj K)))) :
    IsIso ((upperStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} a).map
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ q).map (abelianDerivedBaseChangeArrow sq K)))
